title: Predict the order
promptHtml:
Tracker appends its name to a shared log when it is constructed and again when it is destroyed. Write run_scenario so the log ends up exactly as the checks expect — you are being asked to arrange lifetimes, not to write destructors.

The required log is:

So: a is constructed first and destroyed last, while b and c each live and die inside a’s lifetime, one after the other.
hints:
The starter produces +a +b +c -c -b -a: all three live to the end of the function, then unwind in reverse.

You cannot destroy an object early by hand. You end its lifetime by ending the block it lives in.

An inner { ... } block is a lifetime boundary. You need two of them.
solutionNotesHtml:
The second call to run_scenario in the checks is not padding. It confirms the objects are genuinely recreated each call — if you had reached for static to control the ordering, the second run would log nothing and the check would catch it.

Introducing a scope purely to bound a lifetime is a real technique, not a trick for exercises. It is how you release a lock, close a file, or free a large buffer at a precise point without waiting for the end of the function.
